parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no trans-specific criminal statute and no entry/document rules, so the visitor's formal status is undefined rather than targeted. But the operative environment is severe and state-adjacent: police are recorded perpetrating violence and harassment on grounds of gender identity, detaining LGBTQI+ people for long periods, and extorting release money by threatening charges; forced anal examinations are documented in same-sex prosecutions (tantamount to torture) and anal-examination reports were used as evidence in a mass trial. Same-sex conduct is criminalised and enforced (a 15-year hard-labour sentence reported in 2024), and a trans visitor read as gender-nonconforming or partnered in a way officials deem same-sex enters that machinery. Official hostility is documented (2022 presidential statement followed by a spike in hate speech and assaults), advocacy is effectively barred, and no working remedy appears. The result sits in the Severe Risk band, above pure administrative exclusion and below regimes showing organised trans-specific sweeps or capital charging.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry, visa, passport or gender-marker rules for trans travellers are sourced; a mismatched document is an open question, not a documented refusal practice.
entry_documents.interaction: Unanswered whether border staff would treat a trans visitor's foreign documents as valid; no evidence of a screening regime aimed at trans travellers.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police perpetrate violence and verbal/physical harassment on grounds of gender identity and sexual orientation, hold LGBTQI+ people in prolonged detention, and threaten charges to extort bribes (fines reportedly raised to roughly $30–$900); forced anal examinations are used to gather evidence in same-sex prosecutions.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented safeguard against police abuse; the 2013 acquittal concerned expression, not custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A trans visitor who is outed to police — through a document check, a complaint, or being read as gender-nonconforming — enters a system where officers are the documented risk and detention can escalate to degrading examination.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State detention and prosecution machinery is documented as hostile: enforced same-sex criminalisation (sentences reported up to 14–15 years with hard labour) and anal-examination evidence used in court; no custody-placement protocol for trans detainees is recorded.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Any state facility encounter risks routing an outed trans visitor into a same-sex-conduct investigation, where placement and examination practices are uncontrolled in the record.

care_services.exposure: LGBTQI+ people are recorded as unable to access healthcare services, with no broad anti-discrimination protections; the national AIDS programme does not address same-sex relationships; no trans-specific care or medication information is sourced.
care_services.protection: The 2014 health-professions Code of Ethics bars discrimination on grounds of sexuality, and 2022 HIV guidelines require serving all adolescents regardless of sexual orientation; neither names gender identity.
care_services.interaction: An outed trans visitor needing care faces documented service denial and no trans-specific pathway, with only narrow sexuality-based professional standards as recourse.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The president's 30 May 2022 statement opposing LGBTQI+ protections was followed by a documented spike in hate speech, threats and assaults; public advocacy is effectively barred and a senior official in 1998 called for arrests of gay-rights promoters.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No credible government effort to rescind discriminatory laws; the 2013 freedom-of-expression acquittal was contested by the government and not shown to operate in practice.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing licenses street hostility, raising both the chance an outed visitor is reported or confronted and the likelihood police side with accusers.

minors_guardians.exposure: Penal-code section 158(3) creates a same-sex-specific offence for minors (community service or counselling), an asymmetry with opposite-sex minors; no trans-specific minor rule is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a gender-nonconforming minor faces an undefined risk that a minor's presentation or conduct could be read into this provision; visitor application is unstated.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Mob attacks are documented (2014 neighbourhood apprehension of two suspected lesbians; 2015 mob attack reportedly including three police officers); LGBTQI+ people face societal violence and most remain closeted for fear of targeting.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented functioning recourse; the 2015 case shows police among the perpetrators.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: An outed trans visitor has no realistic protective response to draw on; police involvement in a mob is itself documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No credible government effort to rescind discriminatory laws; the government contested the one 2013 acquittal; advocacy organisations cannot register and assembly on these matters is nonexistent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A 2013 Magistrate and High Court ruling upheld freedom of expression in a decriminalisation advocacy case.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: The single judicial pushback is narrow and unextended; a trans visitor has no documented avenue to challenge police abuse, extortion or examination.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's register produces exclusion and humiliation without arrest; here the dossier documents enforced imprisonment for same-sex conduct, police violence on gender identity, and forced anal examinations, so this case is materially worse.

Kestrel Isles has discretionary secondary screening and refusal of entry but no documented imprisonment or torture-adjacent examinations; here the severity after discovery is far higher, placing this well below.
Meridia trains border officers and has a tribunal with brief detention and compensation; nothing comparable exists here — no remedy is shown operating for trans or LGBTQI+ people.

Saruth shows months of pretrial custody with beatings, medical neglect and capital ambiguity; this dossier documents longer prison sentences and degrading examinations but no capital charging, so it sits somewhat above that tier.

parsed.synthesis: No trans-specific statute or document rule is documented, but that absence is not protection. The operative regime enforces same-sex criminalisation with prison terms, uses forced anal examinations as evidence, and police are documented perpetrators of gender-identity-based violence and extortion. Official framing (the 2022 presidential statement) tracks a documented spike in hate speech and assaults, and advocacy is barred. Remedies are effectively nil: one narrow 2013 expression ruling, contested by the government. An outed trans visitor therefore faces police risk, potential detention and examination, and no working recourse — a Severe Risk profile, not the exclusion-only or protection-operating tiers.
